title: Distinct equal occurrences
scenario: Two CSV records have byte-identical cells but different locators.
expected: Preserve two source occurrences until an authorized duplicate decision explicitly combines them; content hashing cannot erase occurrence identity.

title: Whitespace is a value
scenario: A legal name has leading space while an ID has trailing space and no approved trim step.
expected: Preserve both exact values. Applying a field-specific approved trim changes only that field and leaves lineage.

title: Unicode normalization collision
scenario: Two identifiers differ only by composed/decomposed accent sequences.
expected: Do not merge them through an unapproved global normalization. A selected normalization records the resulting collision as an identity decision.

title: Negative zero and scale
scenario: Decimal strings -0.00, 0 and 001.20 occur in different semantic fields.
expected: Preserve lexical identity fields; numerical output follows an explicit scale/sign policy. No incidental JSON-number round trip.

title: Locale grammar ambiguity
scenario: 1.234 appears with conflicting locale evidence and could mean one point two three four or one thousand two hundred thirty-four.
expected: Withhold conversion until the declared grammar resolves meaning; no majority vote silently changes minority values.

title: Valid low historical year
scenario: Date 0099-01-02 enters every supported date-only primitive.
expected: Output exactly the same year with independent calendar truth; never use the JavaScript 0–99 constructor shortcut.

title: Excel calendar endpoints
scenario: Serials 59, 60 and 61 use the 1900 system, and the same integers use the 1904 system.
expected: 59 maps to 1900-02-28, 60 has no Gregorian date, 61 maps to 1900-03-01; the 1904 profile uses its own epoch without copying the false leap day.

title: DST missing hour
scenario: 2026-03-08 02:30 in America/New_York lacks an offset.
expected: Mark a nonexistent local time as unresolved/error under the selected policy; never silently shift it to another hour.

title: Required versus empty target field
scenario: A required-on-create target field is present as an empty string.
expected: Evaluate actual importer semantics and block invalid creation; presence of a column is not a valid required value.

title: Formula injection as data
scenario: A CSV value starts with =, +, - or @ and is viewed in a spreadsheet-compatible report.
expected: Keep source meaning in the machine data contract while generating a separately safe human-view artifact; no blanket prefix that corrupts CRM import values.

title: Duplicate ZIP path aliases
scenario: XLSX entries differ only through normalized separators or case where the parser resolves them identically.
expected: Reject ambiguous part identity before expansion; no overwrite-by-extraction-order.

title: XML entity expansion
scenario: A workbook relationship/XML part references an external entity.
expected: Reject or parse with external resolution disabled; assert zero DNS/HTTP/file fetch.

title: XLSX absent cached formula result
scenario: A formula cell is selected as a required import field but has no cached result.
expected: Require a new trusted export or explicit exclusion; do not calculate arbitrary formulas or treat the formula text as its value.

title: Conjunctive upload envelope
scenario: A 1.9GB XLSX expands to a 1.1GiB individual XML part while total expansion stays below 20GiB.
expected: Block under the per-part limit despite passing compressed-file and total limits; explain CSV/split alternative.

title: Width times cell size
scenario: Many individually valid cells combine into a decoded record larger than 8MiB.
expected: Enforce the record envelope before allocation grows; a 1MiB cell limit alone is insufficient.

title: Skewed exact join
scenario: A large child edge set points to one merged parent cluster.
expected: Use bounded indexing/spill and an independent edge count; no Cartesian explosion or dropped edges.

title: Hidden release asset mismatch
scenario: Source tar and npm package share a version label but one contains a changed compiled helper.
expected: Compare actual bytes and consumer installation; version text cannot establish equivalence.

title: Native ID from another account
scenario: A plausible HubSpot Record ID comes from another portal.
expected: Block foreign-instance identity even when its textual shape is valid.

title: Identifier precedence side effect
scenario: A Contact update contains both Record ID and a secondary email.
expected: Require the dedicated approved effect and real importer qualification; no accidental primary-email replacement.

title: Association add versus replace
scenario: An existing relationship label is present and the file supplies a new label.
expected: Compare export-back to the selected add/replace intent; additive importer behavior cannot certify replacement.

title: Salesforce relationship depth
scenario: A child file uses a grandparent dotted reference unsupported by the selected import mode.
expected: Reject at compilation; a syntactically plausible field path is not capability.

title: Null marker is literal data
scenario: A text field legitimately contains #N/A while the selected importer uses that token to clear.
expected: Require a representable approved encoding or block that operation; do not silently delete the field.

title: Partial parent success
scenario: Parent stage imports eight of ten rows and two fail.
expected: Validate the exact eight mappings, block child edges depending on failed parents, and preserve all ten source dispositions.

title: Foreign success receipt
scenario: A success CSV from another stage has the same number of rows.
expected: Reject stage/package/instance mismatch before compiling child identities.

title: Receipt retries
scenario: The same stage receipt is uploaded twice, then a different one after finalization.
expected: Identical content is idempotent; differing finalized evidence opens reconciliation rather than overwriting identity.

title: Target enum drift after payment
scenario: An approved allowed value disappears before execution.
expected: Pause affected execution, show scope consequences and provide included repair/refund/new-scope paths without an automatic extra charge.

title: Low-cardinality secret enum
scenario: A destination enum has two customer API tokens as labels.
expected: Exclude L4 values everywhere; cardinality and metadata origin do not relax secrecy.

title: Provider error echoes prompt
scenario: An adapter error includes the full submitted body.
expected: Safe error/telemetry projection removes raw customer content and credentials; secure bounded evidence follows its retention class.

title: Memory cross-client reuse
scenario: One agency has two end clients with similar schemas and conflicting historical decisions.
expected: Select only compatible scoped memory; agency membership alone does not authorize cross-client examples.

title: Keyed symbol scope
scenario: The same personal value appears in two independent attempts.
expected: Within-task equality can be preserved; unrelated attempts must not expose a stable unsalted identity hash.

title: Crash before dispatch
scenario: A task reserves cost then crashes before writing dispatch intent.
expected: Recover under the lease and prove no provider effect before releasing/reusing the reservation.

title: Crash after dispatch intent
scenario: The journal says DISPATCHING and no response exists.
expected: Classify possible liability, reconcile available provider identity and avoid a blind free retry assumption.

title: Crash after response persistence
scenario: Complete response bytes and checksum exist but CONSUMED was not committed.
expected: Validate/read the durable response and continue without a new physical request.

title: Old worker resumes after fence change
scenario: Worker A pauses, B claims a newer fence, then A receives a valid response.
expected: A can contribute reconciled evidence if safe but cannot publish or dispatch under the stale fence.

title: Cancellation at final commit
scenario: Cancellation and SYSTEM_DRAFT promotion contend on the same current version.
expected: Exactly one valid transactional outcome; if cancellation wins, no draft is returned as ready.

title: Budget cost unknown
scenario: A completed response omits usage metadata.
expected: Keep conservative possible cost under UNKNOWN; never count it as zero or free budget.

title: Candidate partition omission
scenario: One of thirty-three useful candidate groups is omitted to fit thirty-two tasks.
expected: Return explicit unresolved scope or a permitted bounded repartition; no complete status with a missing candidate.

title: Duplicate key JSON authority
scenario: The model emits two planHash keys with different values.
expected: Reject before ordinary JSON last-key-wins parsing grants authority.

title: Copied independent run
scenario: Three reports have different filenames but identical invocation/result identities.
expected: Reject independence; verify distinct actual run and provider request provenance.

title: Benchmark contamination
scenario: Expected answer is accidentally included in model context.
expected: Invalidate the affected evaluation and correct the corpus/adapter before new funded runs.

title: Cheap model with unsafe retention
scenario: A low-price endpoint cannot satisfy the project's required data treatment.
expected: Fail eligibility before cost comparison; a cheaper unsafe request is not an optimization.

title: Safe but useless model
scenario: Supported cases abstain while ambiguity cases score perfectly.
expected: Fail supported utility thresholds independently of the safety score.

title: Concurrent final-owner removal
scenario: Two owners each remove the other while reading two active owners.
expected: Serialize the invariant so at least one valid owner remains, or use explicit closure authority.

title: Sealing without audit funding
scenario: All input checks pass but no model budget is available.
expected: Seal may complete; StartAudit is separately blocked without an unfunded provider dispatch.

title: Old valid package after refund
scenario: A worker produces semantically valid output after payment reversal revoked publication.
expected: Retain evidence privately for reconciliation but deny publication under current commercial authority.

title: Queue admission fairness
scenario: One agency submits four paid-ready jobs while another is waiting.
expected: Enforce global active/waiting limits and the documented fair scheduler; do not let one tenant create an unbounded hidden queue.

title: Database owner bypass
scenario: The application test uses a table owner and appears to pass tenant filtering.
expected: Reject the test setup as proof of RLS; run real queries under the production runtime role.

title: Signed URL after role change
scenario: A member loses access after a download token was issued.
expected: Stop new grants immediately and disclose the bounded residual lifetime; do not promise a provider revocation that is unavailable.

title: Metadata-server credential bypass
scenario: An isolated worker obtains its base service-account token and tries a foreign raw prefix.
expected: Actual IAM denies access; passing only through the application broker is insufficient proof.

title: Breakglass renewal after expiry
scenario: An operator reuses an old privileged grant to refresh credentials.
expected: Deny renewal and require a new justified scope; preserve the audit record.

title: Provider session outlives UI
scenario: An application upload reservation expires at twenty-four hours but provider session remains usable.
expected: Tombstone acceptance and cancel the provider session where supported; late objects remain quarantined and are cleaned.

title: Concurrent byte reservation
scenario: Two files each fit remaining revision quota when checked independently.
expected: The aggregate transaction admits only the combination within five billion bytes.

title: Seven-day source with fourteen-day quote
scenario: Quote and source expire on different dates.
expected: Display both; at source expiry checkout is unavailable even if the price remains valid.

title: Staged final delivery near hard cap
scenario: Final stage completes one day before the thirty-day capture hard deadline.
expected: The final seven-day allowance is capped by the hard deadline; show the actual remaining day rather than extending automatically.

title: Waiting customer is not active compute
scenario: A parent stage waits ten days for an agency receipt.
expected: No active heavy job or heartbeat pretends to run; the staged retention deadline continues.

title: Soft-delete policy change
scenario: Bucket policy changes from seven days to zero while old soft-deleted objects remain.
expected: Record actual existing residual expiration; changing policy does not prove prior versions vanished.

title: Restore with deleted audit memory
scenario: Backup contains model memory derived from a deleted project.
expected: Apply tombstones to raw, derived and memory references before allowing reads or provider egress.

title: Boolean coercion
scenario: A request uses the string false instead of boolean false.
expected: Reject structural validation; no coercion/default that changes approval meaning.

title: Unknown privileged request member
scenario: A create-project body includes verified=true and agencyOwner=true.
expected: Reject unknown fields before any state change.

title: Cursor reused across tenants
scenario: A cursor from agency A is submitted for agency B with the same list filter.
expected: Reject cursor scope/signature mismatch without leaking rows or totals.

title: Webhook reordering
scenario: Refund event arrives before delayed capture notification.
expected: Query/reconcile actual provider identities, preserve chronological facts and avoid double-reversing the ledger.

title: Keyboard high-impact approval
scenario: CLEAR confirmation opens a modal and validation returns an error.
expected: Focus remains usable, the error is associated to the exact effect, and no approval occurs on Enter through a hidden default.

title: Stale quote tab
scenario: Two tabs show old/new revisions and the old tab returns from payment approval.
expected: The UI reads durable server state and never offers execution of an unapproved newer revision.

title: Unsaved decisions on navigation
scenario: The agency edits an enum map and leaves the screen before validation.
expected: Show saved/draft status and a recoverable warning; do not silently treat unsaved local edits as approved.

title: Report count denominator
scenario: A flat source creates company/contact projections and multiple relationship files.
expected: Show physical rows, billable source units and output rows separately with understandable definitions.

title: Seller statement after termination
scenario: A former seller retains lawful access to their statement but loses operational access.
expected: Expose only their financial statement/support route, never customer CRM or new prospect tools.

title: Owner finance unknowns
scenario: Dashboard has captures but no verified bank settlement.
expected: Show unknown/unavailable balances and liabilities; no optimistic spendable cash card.

title: Prepared message is not sent
scenario: Assistant creates an outreach draft without explicit send authorization.
expected: State remains DRAFT; no activity log or KPI claims a delivered email.

title: Human-safe versus import artifact
scenario: A malicious spreadsheet prefix needs safe preview escaping.
expected: Keep separately identified safe presentation and machine-import bytes; hashes and instructions identify which artifact to use.

title: White-label legal identity
scenario: Agency branding obscures Kavo's actual contracting/fiscal role.
expected: Preserve required legal identity in terms/invoices; branding cannot fabricate the issuer.

title: Long rejection table
scenario: A report includes many rejected rows with long untrusted values.
expected: Paginate and minimize human output while retaining secure complete machine evidence; no clipped totals or unsafe HTML.

title: Cloud Run disk Preview
scenario: A new disk feature is available but is Preview and not qualified.
expected: Record the changed alternative while retaining Batch until a measured accepted replacement proves the required envelope.

title: Autoscaling exhausts SQL pool
scenario: API max instances doubles without changing per-instance pool size.
expected: Admission/deploy validation detects total connection budget breach before rollout.

title: Restore duplicates notification
scenario: Backup outbox contains a previously sent receipt email.
expected: Reconcile external sent-event identity and avoid another message unless deliberately authorized as a correction.

title: Budget alert arrives late
scenario: Cloud spend grows faster than billing alerts update.
expected: Application reservations and job limits enforce the local grant; alerts are observability rather than the sole cap.

title: Backup without scratch
scenario: A heavy attempt dies and local scratch was never backed up.
expected: Recover only from durable source/checkpoint contracts, or rerun under the same authorized job; do not claim ephemeral intermediate recovery.

title: Founding price arithmetic
scenario: HubSpot 1–50k base is 129500 cents and founding discount is 2500 bps.
expected: Discount 32375; service 97125. No floating-point cent drift.

title: PSP reference arithmetic
scenario: A 97125-cent service capture uses illustrative 540 bps plus 30 cents.
expected: Fee 5275 cents and net 91850 cents under half-up rounding; actual statement fees replace the illustration.

title: First commission arithmetic
scenario: An attributed first service capture is 97125 cents after discount.
expected: Commission 9713 cents; do not subtract the PSP fee from its basis.

title: Repeat and refund arithmetic
scenario: Base HubSpot service gets 5% repeat discount, then 4% commission and a 20000-cent service refund.
expected: Service 123025, original commission 4921, revised commission 4121 and adjustment minus 800 cents.

title: One-cent refund sequence
scenario: Many partial service refunds eventually consume the full captured service amount.
expected: Cumulative entitlement reaches exactly zero; individual rounding cannot leave a commission residue.

title: Tax treatment unresolved
scenario: The operator has not supplied reviewed export-service facts.
expected: No guessed zero VAT or invalid invoice; concrete fiscal-profile action blocks the sale path while independent work continues.

title: Alegra cheapest plan lacks verified API
scenario: A public price page lists an affordable plan but account entitlement is absent.
expected: Do not buy/declare automation ready by assumption; verify entitlement or use the approved lawful bridge.

title: Issued invoice missing from first page
scenario: Provider created an invoice before a timeout; it is beyond the first list page.
expected: Find exact identity using supported query/pagination before creating any replacement.

title: Held funds and withdrawal
scenario: Capture is completed, withdrawal submitted, bank not yet credited.
expected: Show separate capture/held/withdrawn/bank-available facts; no payout from imaginary liquidity.

title: Second project starts repeat benefit
scenario: An agency has one qualifying paid non-fully-refunded project in the lookback.
expected: Apply 5% to its second eligible project, even for a different end client.

title: Tenth prior project threshold
scenario: An agency has ten qualifying prior projects in the 365-day lookback.
expected: Apply 10% to the next eligible quote; count prior projects, not the current capture twice.

title: Twenty-fifth prior project threshold
scenario: An agency has twenty-five qualifying prior projects.
expected: Apply 15% to the next eligible quote and preserve the quoted snapshot through later count changes.

title: Fully refunded previous purchase
scenario: An agency's only prior paid project was fully refunded before new quote calculation.
expected: Exclude it from the active repeat-discount count while preserving historical first-project commission designation.

title: Concurrent founding slots
scenario: Two agencies race for the last of three founding discounts.
expected: Reserve/consume the promotion slot transactionally; no fourth discounted first agency unless a new explicit offer is issued.

title: Promotion is not admission capacity
scenario: Three founding slots are used while safe capacity remains.
expected: Continue selling qualified standard/repeat work within operational limits; do not confuse discount cohort with a total customer cap.

title: Same-band included replacement
scenario: Customer replaces one source before execution without changing priced band.
expected: Require new source validation/approval and consume the one included allowance; no automatic new fee or old authority reuse.

title: Larger replacement scope
scenario: A replacement moves a project from 50000 to 50001 billable units.
expected: Prepare a new price/scope decision and explicit acceptance before another charge; never silently capture the difference.

title: Recurring calendar leap boundary
scenario: First capture is 2028-02-29T15:00:00Z under a twelve-calendar-month term.
expected: Window ends exclusively at 2029-02-28T15:00:00Z under the clamp rule; a purchase at the endpoint is outside automatic residual.

title: Assignment transfer
scenario: Seller B services an agency acquired under seller A's active entitlement.
expected: Keep A's contractual residual; B's new service compensation is separately agreed rather than duplicating or erasing the acquisition pool.

title: First purchase fully refunded
scenario: The historically first qualifying capture is later fully refunded and the agency buys again within the window.
expected: First line becomes zero; the historical first designation and original window do not reset. The later qualifying project uses the recurring rule.

title: Split commission pool
scenario: Two sellers have an agreed 60/40 split of a first-project commission.
expected: Calculate one contractual pool, allocate it deterministically with a remainder rule, and ensure shares sum to the exact pool.

title: Organic purchase after twelve months
scenario: The agency buys after the exclusive recurrence endpoint with no new assistance assignment.
expected: No automatic acquisition residual; earned prior lines remain payable.

title: New work after residual expiry
scenario: A seller is asked to conduct a new demo after the original window.
expected: Create a prospective project-assistance agreement before requiring work; do not condition old rights on unpaid future activity.

title: Termination tail scope
scenario: Seller leaves with two enumerated active opportunities and a thousand scraped prospects.
expected: Only qualifying enumerated opportunities receive the signed ninety-day tail; the list creates no blanket claim.

title: Final staged completion eligibility
scenario: First parent file is ready but final contracted preparation remains incomplete.
expected: Accrual may exist, but the thirty-day payout-eligibility clock does not start from the first stage by default.

title: Partial statement dispute
scenario: One line is disputed and other settled lines are eligible.
expected: Hold only the justified disputed amount, disclose reasons/review date and pay undisputed amounts on the agreed cycle.

title: Changed payout destination
scenario: A seller changes bank details immediately before payout.
expected: Require verified destination-change assurance; no transfer based solely on an unauthenticated email.

title: Negative balance after paid commission
scenario: A legitimate refund reduces an already paid commission.
expected: Post a visible adjustment and apply only the signed lawful offset/recovery policy; do not debit the person's bank without authority.

title: Retainer economics
scenario: Proposed seller compensation is 1000 USD retainer plus 10% of 15000 USD service collections.
expected: Total 2500/15000 is 16.67%, exceeding a 15% planning guard; review economics without claiming the guard is employment law.

title: Qualified outbound with opt-out
scenario: A previously suppressed recipient appears in a new imported prospect batch.
expected: Suppression wins before scheduling or drafting an authorized send; no duplicate-list bypass.

title: Seller overpromises import success
scenario: A proposal claims guaranteed full CRM migration for an unqualified object.
expected: Block/correct the claim and route the scope through capability qualification; do not sell a promise from a product aspiration.

title: Five real projects without sufficient coverage
scenario: Revenue exists but one supported mode and repeat use remain unobserved.
expected: Keep capability/operating maturity labels scoped to actual evidence; revenue alone does not prove every product path.

title: Unknown company assets
scenario: No observed domain, merchant, tax ID or corporate bank exists.
expected: Keep factual fields unknown and prepare exact personal actions; do not manufacture an entity or buy from assumed availability.

title: Contractor label versus actual control
scenario: The proposed seller role imposes fixed hours, exclusivity and subordination.
expected: Require actual local classification review and budget the lawful arrangement before engagement.

title: Agency processor chain
scenario: The agency is itself processing on an end client's instructions.
expected: Record the actual chain, permitted subprocessors/transfers and data authority; a generic controller checkbox is insufficient.

title: Scale without bottleneck evidence
scenario: Revenue improves but measured queue, CPU and support remain healthy.
expected: Do not add fixed capacity by calendar alone; choose a concrete higher-value use or preserve available funds.

title: Gate evidence copied to new image
scenario: Source is unchanged but dependency/image digest differs.
expected: Review transitive impact and invalidate affected evidence; identical source text is not identical candidate.

title: Harness crash treated as rejection
scenario: The test runner crashes before invoking the public API.
expected: Record HARNESS_ERROR, repair the harness and rerun; do not count a detected sabotage or product refusal.

title: Bare Claude report
scenario: Miguel provides only a final report without asking for an audit.
expected: The assistant observes/reviews the subject, updates state and prepares the next concrete mandate automatically.

title: Active mandate survives edition change
scenario: Claude is still running the previously delivered repair prompt.
expected: Preserve its clock and scope until safe transition, then apply R2 prospectively.

title: New IC main with repair claims
scenario: Remote main advanced to a commit claiming more tests.
expected: Record observation and claims separately; do not mark the repairs independently accepted without review.

title: Personal action with guessed UI
scenario: An action card names a stale menu or nonexistent account.
expected: Materialize from current observable state and perform technical preparation before asking Miguel for the irreducible act.

title: Deadline reached with only technical deployment
scenario: The service is reachable but cannot lawfully charge, issue documents or deliver/support the promised scope.
expected: Do not relabel it production to satisfy the date; record the shortfall and precise recovery.

title: Revenue mistaken for wealth
scenario: A monthly dashboard treats gross captures, held funds and a hypothetical valuation as Miguel's liquid wealth.
expected: Separate gross service revenue, liabilities, settled company cash, lawful distributions and personal assets.

title: No three-month reserve rule
scenario: A saleable qualified launch fits actual current funding but lacks three months of idle cash.
expected: Do not impose an arbitrary reserve prerequisite; protect actual near-term obligations and approved exposure.

title: Year-five forecast without buyers
scenario: A scenario assumes one hundred agencies and four projects each.
expected: Label the multiplication as a scenario, attach acquisition/capacity/margin conditions and spend only from real authorized funds.

title: Soft extension inside hard cap
scenario: An agency requests 72 hours before expiry and the hard cap is only 24 hours away.
expected: Grant at most the remaining 24 hours, disclose the exact endpoint and consume the one extension; never move the hard cap.

title: Second or late extension
scenario: A project already used its extension or requests it after expiry.
expected: Reject without reviving access, resetting clocks or changing a tombstone.

title: Extension versus deletion race
scenario: A pre-expiry extension and deletion/expiry compete on the same retention version.
expected: One valid transaction wins; a later extension cannot undo committed deletion authority.

title: Restore after acknowledged extension
scenario: A backup predates a valid acknowledged soft extension.
expected: Apply the current durable retention-authority journal before cleanup so the restored old deadline cannot prematurely delete promised data.

title: Founding quote reservation
scenario: A binding founding quote is issued while one promotion slot remains.
expected: Reserve that one slot through the original fourteen-day quote expiry; previews reserve nothing, quote IDs do not renew it, and capture uncertainty prevents unsafe release.

title: Local fiscal adapter boundary
scenario: A domestic taxable sale and an export-claimed sale share the same payment amount but different evidence.
expected: The adapter cannot infer export exemption from currency or foreign email; emit the selected reviewed fiscal treatment or block issuance, preserving capture reconciliation.

title: Uncertain email submission
scenario: Gmail accepts a message but the transport response is lost.
expected: Record SEND_UNCERTAIN and require scoped reconciliation; do not resend automatically or claim inbox delivery.

title: Opt-out wins dispatch race
scenario: A recipient opts out after grant creation and before dispatcher claim.
expected: Current suppression blocks the send; a sealed campaign grant cannot override a later refusal.

title: No cold outreach through transactional provider
scenario: A sales draft for an unsolicited prospect selects the Resend route.
expected: Reject the route despite valid API credentials and spare quota; preserve the draft for a genuinely permitted channel.

title: Sender consent revoked
scenario: A seller OAuth grant is revoked with queued drafts.
expected: Stop future dispatch for that sender, preserve uncertain/past activity and never borrow the owner identity.

title: Notification quota and authenticity
scenario: A notification campaign approaches its observed quota and a forged webhook claims delivery.
expected: Reserve essential capacity or raise a funded action, reject unauthenticated events and keep authenticated in-app state available.

title: Expired login and legal acceptance
scenario: An invitation expires while a user reads a newly versioned legal agreement.
expected: Authentication recovery does not revive the invitation or silently accept changed terms; show the current required action without leaking account existence.

title: Obsolete seller resource
scenario: A seller opens an old offer sheet that promises an unavailable CRM capacity.
expected: Show superseded status and current safe resource; prevent its use in a new approved draft while preserving historical records.

title: Fractional-cent discount order
scenario: A synthetic arithmetic basis of 1002 cents receives a 25 percent discount.
expected: Round the 250.5-cent discount to 251, then subtract for 751 net cents. Rounding the complementary 75 percent to 752 is wrong. This vector does not create a new advertised price band.

title: Late earlier capture keeps first designation
scenario: Project P is durably confirmed first; a later authenticated event proves Q completed at the provider earlier.
expected: Keep P as historical first and Q subsequent; preserve actual timestamps and use the verified recurring cutoff without granting a second 10 percent pool.

title: Residual exclusive cutoff and delayed notice
scenario: Two subsequent captures occur one second before and exactly at the local twelve-month endpoint, both notified later.
expected: The first can qualify at 4 percent; the endpoint capture does not. Quote or notification time cannot replace verified provider completion.

title: Controlled banking calendar
scenario: A September statement uses a test calendar excluding weekends and 2026-10-12.
expected: Compute 2026-10-07 as fifth and 2026-10-15 as tenth business day. Production must bind a verified current banking calendar; the fixture is not a live holiday authority.

title: Two actual captures for one obligation
scenario: One order receives two different verified full captures, while a separate delivery repeats one capture event.
expected: Account for both real captures and the excess-refund obligation, deduplicate repeated events, keep one service entitlement and cap commission basis to the service obligation.

title: Agency rename versus legal consolidation
scenario: A buyer changes display name/email; a separate holding-company agency requests shared pricing.
expected: A rename preserves history, rights and tenant identity. Consolidation requires an explicit reviewed relationship decision and cannot merge datasets or erase attribution.
